comparisons.peer_topic: Revenue recognition for non-recurring engineering (NRE) contracts
comparisons.peer_summary: NRE contract revenue is generally recognized over time based on the input method of costs incurred, as customers consume services during development. Revenue for NRE contracts not meeting over-time criteria is recognized at a point in time when services are complete.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Broadcom recognize revenue over time for custom development and non-recurring engineering (NRE) contracts. AMD explicitly states that revenue from custom products and development services is recognized over time, accounting for 8% of its 2024 revenue. Broadcom similarly discloses that the majority of its NRE contracts, which involve developing custom chips or accelerating new chip development, meet over-time recognition criteria and are measured using an input method based on costs incurred. While both use cost-based input methods for over-time recognition, AMD quantifies the materiality of this revenue stream (8% in 2024), whereas Broadcom qualifies it as 'the majority' of NRE revenue without providing a specific percentage of total revenue.

sentences.text: Revenue recognized over time associated with custom products and development services accounted for approximately 8%, 25% and 24% of the Company's revenue in 2024, 2023 and 2022, respectively.
The majority of our NRE contract revenues meet the over time criteria.
As such, revenue is recognized over the development period with the measure of progress using the input method based on costs incurred to total cost as the services are provided.

comparisons.peer_summary: Intel recognizes net product revenue when performance obligations are satisfied via transfer of control, with substantially all revenue from product sales. Revenue is recognized at shipment or delivery based on shipping terms, even when products include interdependent software components accounted for as a combined performance obligation.
comparisons.comparison: The target (AMD) discloses a specific revenue percentage recognized over time (8% in 2024) for custom products, whereas Intel (INTC) discloses that substantially all of its revenue is derived from product sales recognized at a point in time (upon shipment or delivery). While both operate in the semiconductor industry and recognize revenue based on the transfer of control or satisfaction of performance obligations, Intel's primary model is point-in-time recognition for products, contrasting with AMD's explicit disclosure of a significant over-time revenue component for custom development. Intel does not disclose a comparable percentage for over-time recognized revenue in this context.

comparisons.peer_topic: Revenue Recognition Policy and Contract Terms
comparisons.peer_summary: Revenue is recognized at a point in time when control transfers, primarily for short-term contracts at fixed prices, though some contracts have performance obligations extending beyond one year.
comparisons.comparison: Micron (MU) states that revenue is primarily recognized at a point in time when control of goods is transferred, consistent with AMD's general product sales model, but contrasts with AMD's specific disclosure of 8% of revenue recognized over time for custom development. Micron acknowledges that while substantially all contracts are short-term fixed-price, some performance obligations extend beyond one year, implying some over-time recognition, but it does not quantify this portion or explicitly define a category like 'custom products and development services' with a specific revenue percentage as AMD does.

comparisons.peer_topic: Revenue recognition for license and development arrangements
comparisons.peer_summary: Revenue from license and development services with significant customization is recognized as a single performance obligation over the development period, measured by actual costs incurred as a percentage of estimated total costs, with losses recorded when probable.
comparisons.comparison: AMD and NVIDIA both recognize revenue over time for custom product and development services where customers receive benefits as work progresses. AMD discloses that custom products and development services account for approximately 8% of its 2024 revenue and are recognized over time. NVIDIA similarly recognizes revenue from license and development services with significant customization as a single performance obligation over the development period. Both companies utilize a cost-to-cost approach (input method based on costs incurred) to measure progress toward completion for these over-time revenue streams.
